title.narrative: Strengthened capacities of tripartite constituents to facilitate the transition of workers and enterprises to formality

description.narrative:
The informal economy remains a critical source of employment and livelihoods for most people but is commonly associated with vulnerable employment, low and unstable earnings, unsafe working conditions, weak representation, and limited access to social protection, finance, markets and business development services. The 2025 Zimbabwe Economic Census confirmed the prevalence of informality and dominance by micro-enterprises, accounting for approximately 76% of operational business establishments, reinforcing the scale of the challenge and the need for coordinated, inclusive responses. The is increased emphasis on transforming the informal economy into a driver of inclusive growth, productivity and decent work.
Through the DWCP for Zimbabwe the ILO supports tripartite constituents to design and implement integrated strategies that enable a gradual and inclusive transition to formality as outlined in ILO Recommendation 204 (Transition from the Informal to Formal Economy). This includes supporting the adoption and implementation of a National Formalisation Strategy. The strategy promotes partnerships among social partners, the private sector, civil society and international organizations to leverage resources and expertise. This work benefits informal workers and enterprises, particularly women and youth, and contributes to improved working conditions, productivity and access to social protection.
ILO support focuses on simplifying regulatory and taxation frameworks, introducing incentives for registration and compliance, and extending decent work principles-such as rights at work, occupational safety and health, social dialogue, and the coverage of social protection systems. The approach also focuses on expanding access to finance, markets and quality business development services; strengthening skills development and productivity; and improving linkages between informal and formal value chains.
